violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: In the M3 Turbo Air 2DR UPR cooler, raw chicken was being stored above ready to eat pork belly.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL RAW FOODS NEED TO BE STORE BELOW READY TO EAT FOODS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE THE RAW CHICKEN TO BELOW THE READY TO EAT PORK BELLY.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: pork spare ribs (125F) and cooked sweet potatoes (121F) in the 1DR UPR hot holding unit were not temping properly at 135F or above.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL HOT FOODS NEED TO BE HOT HOLDING AT 135F OR ABOVE. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE THE SPARE RIBS AND SWEET POTATOES BACK TO THE OVEN TO HEAT TO A TEMP OF 135F OR HIGHER BEFORE PLACING THEM BACK ON THE 1DR UPR HOT HOLDING UNIT TO HOT HOLD. BLUE PEARL BUFFET (Inspection Date: 08/03/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: Frozen imitation crab was being stored at room temp on a prep table to thaw.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE 3 PROPER WAYS TO THAW FOODS. 1) COOK STRAIGHT FROM FROZEN 2) PLACE IN REFRIGERATOR FROM FREEZER UNTIL FULLY THAWED 3) PLACE FOOD UNDER RUNNING WATER OF 70F OR BELOW UNTIL FULLY THAWED. PIC MOVED IMITATION CRAB TO COOLER TO PROPERLY THAW.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoop for white rice on buffet line was being stored in still water of 61F. A knife was being stored in still water at 59F at the sushi prep top cooler.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL INUSE UTENSILS NEED TO BE STORED IN HOT WATER OF AT LEAST 135F BETWEEN EACH USE. PIC REPLACED THE WATER WITH WARM WATER OF AT LEAST 135F.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Wash Temp for Hot Water Warewashing Machines
violations.observation: The wash water temperature of the hot water sanitizing warewashing machine is not meeting the manufacturer's specifications. The minimum temperature was 160F while the actual temperature was 155F.
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than: 1) 165F for a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 2) 150F for a stationary rack, dual temperature machine, 3) 160F for a single tank, conveyor, dual temperature machine, or 4) 150F for a multitank, conveyor, multitemperature machine. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THE HIGH TEMP DISH MACHINE MUST REACH A MINIMUM TEMP OF 160F IN ORDER TO PROPERLY SANITIZE DISHES. PIC CALLED MAINTENANCE FOR THE MACHINE AND WAS ABLE TO GET THE DISH WASHER TEMPERATURE FIXED BEFORE THE END OF THE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw pork was being stored under raw chicken in the walk-in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL RAW FOODS IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR NEED TO BE ORGANIZED BY COOK TEMPERATURES IN ORDER TO COOK OFF ANY BACTERIA THAT MAY OCCUR IF CONTAMINATION HAPPENS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE REARRANGE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR BASED ON COOK TEMPERATURES. A BLUE PEARL BUFFET (Inspection Date: 01/03/2025) Page 2 of 3
